sections.title: What MUDRA is and how it was formed

blocks.text: **MUDRA** stands for **Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency**. Despite the word 'Bank' in its popular name, it is a **public sector financial institution** that does not lend directly to small shopkeepers. It provides low-cost refinance to **micro-finance institutions (MFIs)** and **non-banking financial companies (NBFCs)**, which then pass credit on to micro and small enterprises (MSMEs).

blocks.title: Formation of MUDRA (2015)
items: Setting up of the agency is announced in the **Union Budget for FY 2015-16**.
MUDRA is registered as a company under the **Companies Act, 2013**.
Registered with the **RBI** as a **Non-Banking Finance Institution**.
MUDRA is **formally launched**; the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) begins alongside it.

blocks.title: Key terms
rows: Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency, set up to develop the micro-enterprise sector.
Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana, the scheme under which collateral-free loans are given to non-agricultural micro and small businesses.
Money MUDRA lends to banks, NBFCs and MFIs so that they can lend further to small units.
The motto of MUDRA: reach small businesses that regular banks usually do not finance.

blocks.title: Two dates, one day apart
blocks.text: **7 April 2015** = registered with RBI as an NBFI. **8 April 2015** = formal launch. Examiners like to use the wrong day as a distractor.

blocks.title: Order of the 2015 milestones
blocks.phrase: Budget Feb, Company Mar, RBI 7th, Launch 8th – 'B-C-R-L' (Big Companies Raise Loans).
letters: RBI registration as NBFI on 7 April 2015

blocks.text: MUDRA's main objective is to **develop the micro-enterprise sector** by giving various supports, most importantly financial support in the form of **refinance**, so that the goal of 'funding the unfunded' is achieved. The Government of India later added more tasks to its list.

blocks.title: Roles assigned to MUDRA
items: **Monitor PMMY data** by managing a web portal that captures lending in detail.
**Facilitate guarantees** for loans granted under PMMY.
Take up other activities that the Government assigns from time to time.

blocks.title: How it works on the ground
items: It serves small entrepreneurs **outside the reach of regular banks**, using **last-mile agents**.
The target group is about **5.77 crore (57.6 million)** small businesses identified through the **NSSO survey**.
Only about **4%** of these businesses were getting finance from regular banks.
MUDRA aims to ensure that its clients **do not fall into indebtedness** and are lent to responsibly.
It is also meant to oversee and support the micro-finance institutions that lend to such units.

blocks.title: Not a retail bank
blocks.text: MUDRA does **not** open accounts or give loans to the public directly. Borrowers apply to banks, NBFCs or MFIs; MUDRA refinances those lenders.

At the start MUDRA functioned as a **non-banking financial company** and a **subsidiary of SIDBI** (Small Industries Development Bank of India). It was later made into a **separate company**. The Credit Guarantee Fund reduces the credit risk for banks and other lenders that finance micro units.

blocks.title: How credit reaches a micro unit
Remember the two big numbers
blocks.phrase: '20 and 3' – capital ₹20,000 crore, guarantee fund ₹3,000 crore. Convert billions by dividing by 10 to get thousands of crore.
blocks.note: ₹10 billion = ₹1,000 crore, so 200 billion = 20,000 crore and 30 billion = 3,000 crore.

blocks.text: MUDRA classifies its clients into **three categories** that signal the **stage of growth and funding need** of the micro unit. The maximum loan allowed depends on the category.

blocks.title: PMMY categories
headers: Share of the additional ₹1 trillion fund
rows: Above ₹5 lakh and up to ₹10 lakh

blocks.title: Loan size grows with the business
Baby, Teen, Adult
blocks.phrase: Shishu = Baby (₹50K), Kishor = Teenager (₹5 lakh), Tarun = Young adult (₹10 lakh). Loan doubles roughly with each life stage.
blocks.note: Allocation of the extra fund goes 40-35-25: the smaller the loan, the bigger the share.

blocks.title: MUDRA refinances loans to units such as
Spelling
blocks.text: 'Kishor' is also written 'Kishore' in many papers. Both refer to the middle category with the ₹5 lakh ceiling.

sections.title: Who lends, monitoring and the MUDRA Card

blocks.text: PMMY was launched together with MUDRA, and the Government issued detailed guidelines to all **banks and microfinance institutions**. Loans under PMMY are given by scheduled commercial banks, NBFCs and MFIs. A **payments bank** cannot lend, so it is not among the PMMY lenders.

blocks.title: Monitoring and the card
rows: MUDRA was made responsible for monitoring the programme by collecting information regularly. Its web portal captures lending data under PMMY in a granular way.
A **debit card** issued against the MUDRA loan account for the **working-capital portion** of the loan.
Valid up to the due date of the **overdraft (OD) limit**.
Allows multiple withdrawals and credits so the borrower can manage working capital efficiently.

blocks.title: Payments bank odd one out
blocks.text: If a question asks which institution CANNOT give MUDRA loans, think: commercial banks, NBFCs and MFIs can lend; **payments banks** accept deposits only and cannot extend loans.

blocks.title: Who may lend under PMMY
blocks.phrase: 'B-N-M' – Banks, NBFCs, MFIs lend; Payments banks can't (they only pay).

revision: MUDRA = Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency; a public sector financial institution giving refinance, not retail loans.
Announced in the Union Budget FY 2015-16 (Feb 2015); registered as a company in March 2015 under the Companies Act 2013.
Registered with RBI as an NBFI on 7 April 2015 and formally launched on 8 April 2015.
Main goal: 'funding the unfunded' micro enterprises; set up under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY).
Initial capital ₹200 billion (₹20,000 crore); Credit Guarantee Fund ₹30 billion (₹3,000 crore).
Began as an NBFC and subsidiary of SIDBI, later made a separate company.
About 5.77 crore small businesses targeted (NSSO survey); only about 4% had access to regular bank finance.
Shishu: up to ₹50,000 (40% of extra fund); Kishor: up to ₹5 lakh (35%); Tarun: up to ₹10 lakh (25%).
PMMY loans are collateral-free for non-agricultural micro and small businesses.
Lenders: scheduled commercial banks, NBFCs and MFIs; payments banks cannot lend.
MUDRA monitors PMMY through a web portal and can facilitate guarantees for PMMY loans.
MUDRA Card: debit card on the loan account for the working-capital portion; valid 5 years; limit valid up to OD due date.
